comments.note:
[Pedagogy audit v2 · New question to decide] For the type count gap (invert-square-area-scaling). Comparison score 45, between A4 and A5: Part a needs a square root of an algebraic fraction. Part b needs a subtraction in context. Part c needs the sum of two sides, then squaring. These are linked steps that are only moderately signposted.
Proposed question: A square garden bed has side length $s$ metres. A square paving slab has area $\dfrac{4s^2}{9}$ square metres.
a) Write an expression for the side length of the paving slab.
b) Write an expression for the area of the garden bed that is not covered when the slab is laid inside it.
c) A new square has a side length equal to the sum of the side lengths of the garden bed and the slab. Write an expression for its area.
(with a diagram)
Answers: a) $\dfrac{2s}{3}$ metres; b) $\dfrac{5s^2}{9}$ square metres; c) $\dfrac{25s^2}{9}$ square metres

[Pedagogy audit v2 · New question to decide] For the type count gap (generalise-repeated-area-scaling). Comparison score 55, between A5 and p21-q7: Two different ratios have to be applied to the sides and multiplied. Repeating this gives an area factor of 1/2 each time, and part d asks for a general n-th term, which needs the index laws.
Proposed question: A poster has length $l$ cm and width $w$ cm. Each copy of the poster has a length that is three-quarters of the length of the previous poster and a width that is two-thirds of the width of the previous poster.
a) Write an expression for the length and width of copy 1.
b) Write an expression for the area of copy 1.
c) Write an expression for the area of copy 2.
d) Write an expression for the area of copy $n$.
(with a diagram)
Answers: a) Length: $\dfrac{3l}{4}$; width: $\dfrac{2w}{3}$.; b) $\dfrac{lw}{2}$; c) $\dfrac{lw}{4}$; d) $\dfrac{lw}{2^n}$
